steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: The development gap is the difference in levels of wealth and standard of living between the richest and poorest countries in the world. Reducing this gap requires strategies that address economic, social, and political inequality.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Investment is when money is put into a country's economy to generate future returns. This can come from foreign direct investment (FDI), governments, or international organisations.

steps.title: Key Point
steps.body: Countries typically develop through the Clark-Fisher model: primary sector (farming, mining) → secondary sector (manufacturing) → tertiary sector (services) → quaternary sector (research, IT). Moving up this chain increases GNI per head.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Tourism is travel for pleasure or business. It is one of the world's largest industries and can bring significant income and employment to LICs and NEEs.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use a named case study with specific data when evaluating strategies For "how far do you agree" questions, discuss multiple strategies and compare their effectiveness Remember to consider both advantages AND disadvantages for every strategy Use the Jamaica case study with specific statistics for tourism questions Key terms to use: economic leakage, intermediate technology, Fairtrade premium, microcredit, HIPC Higher mark questions require evaluation - don't just describe, assess how effective each strategy is
